text:
Maria H: Hey team, noticed a regression in prompt-cache hit behavior after last night's runtime/kernel heuristics push + new quant profile. :frowning: 92% -> ~60% hit for short user prompts (common chat flows). p95 latency for those flows climbed 22ms -> 37ms.

Aj O: :eyes: do we have a quick diff between kernel selection tables? Could be different kernel variant for short seqs.

Maria H: I grabbed the build IDs and kernel hints from production traces. Looks like the scheduler picked `kernel_v3b_vec` for batch size 1 on the upgraded image, previously we had `kernel_v3a_scalar` for those same traces. Suspect the kernel change + quant profile changed fingerprinting.

Devon L: Any evidence it's key canonicalization vs tokenization? Sometimes tokenization changes re-order whitespace which affects cache keys.

Maria H: Good call. I compared tokenizer outputs for a sample of ~2k requests: canonicalized tokens match, but the binding of pad/null bytes and a trailing BOS marker differ in one of the model variants after quantized compile. So keys that used to be identical now differ by a final control token.

Priya K: Can you paste the small repro script you used? I can run a local trace with the new kernels + quant profile.

Maria H: Repro steps below (super short):
```
# repro snippet
curl -s -X POST https://redwood-int/api/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DEV_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"open-rw-v3b-q","prompt":"Hello\nHow are you?","max_tokens":32}'
# capture response.token_ids then compare prefix-key from runtime log
```

Maria H: Attached runtime log lines (obfuscated):
```
[prod] trace=abc123 build=2026-03-12 kernel_hint=kernel_v3b_vec kv_key=0x7f2a9c.. hit=false
[prod] trace=abc124 build=2026-03-12 kernel_hint=kernel_v3a_scalar kv_key=0x7f2a9c.. hit=true
```

Aj O: kv_key looks same in hex snippet, are we sure it's the same canonicalization? maybe the runtime salts the key with compilation fingerprint now. Any build_id mismatch between cache nodes?

Maria H: Bingo — the cache now includes a 4-byte compile fingerprint appended to the key for cache safety in this deploy. The old keys omitted it. That means old prefixes are missed until we backfill or relax the fingerprinting rule. I missed that change in the heuristic PR.

Devon L: Oof. Why was fingerprint appended? I thought we used compatibility mapping for kernel variants. PR comment said "safety fingerprint for kernel/quant parity" but should be optional.

Priya K: I can push a fast rollback to the prior kernel heuristic (revert the fingerprint append) for the affected tier. Will that be acceptable short-term?

Maria H: Yes please. For surface-level mitigation we can also enable key-normalization that strips trailing control tokens and the 4-byte fingerprint when doing a lookup (fall back mode). But rollout/revert is faster.

perf-bot: CI perf-alert: prompt-cache hit-rate drop detected for service=runtime region=us-west-2 delta=-32pct p95-latency +15ms (since 2026-03-15T03:10Z).

Aj O: If we rollback, be careful with cross-compat: some nodes will still have keys with fingerprint appended and lookups may hit later once the old traffic ages out. Need a migration plan: either backfill keys without fingerprint or run dual-lookup for 24h (check both forms).

Maria H: Proposed plan: 1) rollback kernel-heuristics change in canary (5% traffic) now. 2) enable dual-lookup (try with-and-without fingerprint) for 12h. 3) run a background backfill job to re-hash hot prefixes without fingerprint. 4) followup: update PR to make fingerprint opt-in per model family.

Devon L: Sounds good. I'll own the backfill job. Need an estimate: hot set ~120k prefixes, should be < 2h with our backfill runners.

Priya K: Rolling back canary now. Deploy ID: deploy-2026-03-15-kernelheuristic-revert. Monitor link: https://internal.redwood/perf/dash/traceid=abc123 :thumbsup:

Maria H: Thanks. After the canary revert and enabling dual-lookup we saw hit-rate recover from 60% -> 88% in 20 minutes on canary traffic. p95 dropped back toward 24ms.

Aj O: Follow-up items: add unit test for key-generation that asserts fingerprint opt-in, update release notes, and add an alert that flags kernel->key fingerprint toggles.

Maria H: I'll open the follow-up tickets and a short postmortem. Big thanks for the quick responses. :raised_hands:
